result: 6/6 pages succeeded on the SECOND attempt (see bug_found_and_worked_around)

bug_found_and_worked_around.symptom: first attempt, using device: "auto" (production_baseline_config v1), crashed ALL 6/6 pages at the table_transformer stage: RuntimeError: Expected one of cpu, cuda, ... device type at start of device string: auto
bug_found_and_worked_around.root_cause: src/doc_extraction/cli.py: resolve_device(config) (which turns "auto" into a concrete cpu/cuda string via select_device()) is called ONLY inside cmd_run/cmd_compare (the argparse CLI dispatch functions, lines 339/383) -- process_file() (line 246), the library entrypoint experiments/005_omnidocbench/prepare.py calls directly, never calls resolve_device() at all. The literal string "auto" flows unresolved into TableTransformerBackend(device="auto") (table_backend.py), which calls .to("auto") and crashes -- DoclingBackend tolerated it (layout/ocr stages succeeded), only the table stage failed, which is why the smoke test surfaced this precisely rather than an earlier, more confusing failure.
bug_found_and_worked_around.verified_not_fixed: src/ was NOT modified -- confirmed by git status after this milestone completes (Phase 20). This is a genuine, reproducible, previously-undiscovered production bug, reported here as a finding, not patched.
bug_found_and_worked_around.workaround_used: switched production_baseline_config.yaml from a hand-edited cpu.yaml (device: auto) to an UNMODIFIED copy of configs/gpu.yaml (device: "cuda" literal) -- an EXISTING, already-validated production config for a GPU-clear scenario (validated 2026-09-01 per its own header), not a benchmark-special invention. GPU state re-confirmed CLEAR immediately before this switch.
bug_found_and_worked_around.significance: this means device: "auto" has likely NEVER been exercised end-to-end through TableTransformerBackend via any library-call path in this repository before -- only via the CLI. Flagged as a real, separate bug-fix candidate for a future milestone, out of scope to fix here.
